limitations: Legacy OAuth Apps grant broad, account-wide permissions. GitHub strongly recommends GitHub Apps for granular repository-level access control.

assumptions: Setting up standard GitHub App or OAuth App with read:user, repo scopes

externalWait.publishedRange: Instant activation (no review required for standard public or private usage)

prerequisites.text: GitHub user account with verified email address

steps.title: Decide Between GitHub App vs OAuth App
steps.instructions: Determine your architecture: Choose 'GitHub App' (recommended) for fine-grained repository permissions, bot accounts, and higher API rate limits (5,000/hr per installation). Choose 'OAuth App' only if you strictly need simple user identity federation without repo-specific management.

steps.title: Register Application in Developer Settings
steps.instructions: In GitHub, click your profile avatar > 'Settings' > 'Developer settings'. Click either 'GitHub Apps' or 'OAuth Apps' > 'New App'. Provide Application name, Homepage URL, and Authorization callback URL (e.g. `https://app.example.com/api/auth/callback/github`).
steps.completionCheck: App dashboard displays generated Client ID.

steps.title: Generate Client Secret
steps.instructions: Under 'Client secrets', click 'Generate a new client secret'. Immediately copy the secret string into your secure environment configuration.

steps.title: Configure Webhooks & Scopes (GitHub Apps)
steps.instructions: If using a GitHub App, configure the Webhook URL and Webhook secret to receive asynchronous events (e.g. push, pull_request). Under 'Permissions & events', configure repository and account permissions.

blockers.title: Organization OAuth App Restrictions
blockers.description: If your users belong to an organization with 'Third-party application access restrictions' enabled, an organization owner must grant approval before members can access organizational data.

claims.text: GitHub Apps offer fine-grained permissions per repository, whereas OAuth Apps grant permissions across all repositories accessible by the user.
Callback URLs must be exact matches; wildcards are not permitted on GitHub OAuth registrations.
Client secrets are only displayed once upon creation and cannot be retrieved later.

selectedPassages: GitHub Apps are the officially recommended way to integrate with GitHub because they offer much more granular permissions.
No manual approval is required from GitHub to begin using your app with end users.
